## Changes

### Major (6)
1. U6 · l · `kebteġülsütü` -tü ("having") was dropped from "night-guards" and the plain "night-guards, … guardsman-having" mis-assigned it; l now "eighty night-guards-having, seventy day-watch guardsmen-having". `i` kept (note already hedged).
2. U12 · l · `miṅγad` was left out of l (only "to-thousands"), and `oroγ̇ulqu-ji` was rendered "bringing-in-of" (a genitive) while the note calls -ji the accusative. Now "bringing-in (acc.) decree, thousands to-thousands".
3. U34 · i · "that man shall be blamed, and we shall send him behind our eyes": ereġülüžü is a converb on an accusative object (not a passive), ileje is the hortative "let us send", and "our" is not in the Ming. Now "faulting that man, let us send him behind the eyes, out of sight, to a far land."
4. U36 · i · surulčasu (Ming 共學我, note "let us all learn") was rendered "serve together". Now "Let us learn together, going about within in our presence," (also dropped the invented "thus").
5. U49 · i · The comitative Bügidei-lüġe ("with Tüge's son Bügidei") had been turned into a co-subject. Now "and taking counsel together with Tüge's son Bügidei, let him be."
6. U58, U59, U63, U64 · l, i, n, morph gloss · čerbi was rendered "chamberlain", an identification with no support in the Ming (官名 only) and against the glossary ("meaning of the title not known"). Now untranslated "cherbi" (l, i), morph gloss "cherbi, an office or rank (meaning not known)"; note at U58 rewritten.

## Findings refused
- köġüd-te: glossary lemma is `köġü`, the other entries and the part use `köġün`; left as `köġün` (glossary slip, to be fixed there).
- qorčin kept as one morph although the glossary analyses qor-či-n (marked uncertain there); the reader-visible split is a glossary-side decision.
- aqalažu lemma `aqala-` (glossary entry keyed `aqa`): both are the same analysis (aqa + -la-); kept.
- turγaγ̇ud lemma `turγaγ` / baγ̇atud lemma `baγ̇atur`: glossary lists both variants; left.
- U8 "I alone" and U47 "I selected": subject supplied from context (the speaker is Chinggis); acceptable and noted in U47.
- U14 note "let them be brought in" vs i "let them bring in": both readings of the causative optative; left.
- U68 i "taking charge … let them be the day watch": ambiguous subject but follows l; left.
- U1–U2 note wording "scribe": harmless.
- `ln` / `p: true` are not in the units; the build supplies them (runbook).
